result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and curb ramps with tactile warning surfaces, indicating a prioritized pedestrian environment. A buffered bike lane provides additional separation between the sidewalk and motor vehicle traffic, though the wide one-way street configuration may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Wide one-way travel lane
hazards.description: The wide, straight one-way street can encourage higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are clearly visible to provide explicit crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signal heads with countdown timers to improve pedestrian predictability and safety.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. The environment is generally pedestrian-friendly with clear signals and curb ramps, though parked cars along the curb may impact visibility at the crossing points.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the street edge may block the view of pedestrians for approaching drivers, especially at the start of the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right and left curbs approaching the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a well-marked zebra crosswalk with curb ramps and wide, unobstructed sidewalks. However, the lack of active traffic control and the presence of parked vehicles near the crossing create potential visibility hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk on both sides of the street obstruct the sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs immediately preceding the zebra crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: There are no visible stop signs or signals to regulate vehicle flow at this marked crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection where the crosswalk is located.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

result.summary: The image shows a well-maintained urban street with wide sidewalks and a signalized pedestrian crossing. While basic infrastructure like crosswalks and signals are present, the sidewalk is partially obstructed by utility boxes, and the intersection lacks modern safety features like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Large utility boxes and poles on the left sidewalk reduce the effective width for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Intersection Geometry
hazards.description: The lack of curb extensions increases the unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians.
